source_refs.note: Topic 22.5 (PDF 95); the structures and the scheme are redrawn. The book's scheme puts NaOH over the second arrow with NaCl as a product; the text says the salt is warmed and hydrolysed, so the lesson gives the reaction with water.

blocks.text: Compounds in which a hydroxyl group is bonded to an aromatic ring (an arene) are phenols. The simplest is phenol itself, C6H5OH, also known as carbolic acid, once used in carbolic soap; it is a white crystalline solid. Other examples are 1-naphthol and 2-naphthol, with the -OH group on naphthalene.

blocks.alt: Three structures: phenol, a benzene ring with OH; 2-naphthol, two fused rings with OH at position 2; 1-naphthol, two fused rings with OH at position 1.
blocks.caption: Examples of phenols: phenol, 2-naphthol and 1-naphthol (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 95).

blocks.text: Phenol can be made from phenylamine and nitrous acid (HNO2) in three steps:

items: Nitrous acid is too unstable to store, so it is made in the test tube from sodium nitrite (NaNO2) and dilute hydrochloric acid, kept below 10 C with ice.
Phenylamine reacts with the nitrous acid to form an unstable diazonium salt, benzenediazonium chloride, C6H5N2+ Cl-.
On further warming, phenol is produced as diazonium salt is decomposed (hydrolysed).

blocks.alt: Phenylamine (benzene ring with NH2), with NaNO2 over the arrow and 'HCl, < 10 degrees C' under it, gives benzenediazonium chloride (ring with N+ triple bond N and Cl-), which with NaOH over the arrow gives phenol + NaCl + N2.
blocks.caption: Preparation of phenol from phenylamine (original drawing after the textbook's unnumbered figure on PDF page 95).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed scheme uses NaOH for the last step and gives phenol + NaCl + N2. Phenol is made by warming the diazonium salt solution with water: C6H5N2+ Cl- + H2O -> C6H5OH + N2 + HCl, as the book itself gives in Chapter 24 (PDF page 125). In alkali the phenol would form phenoxide and couple with the remaining diazonium ions to give an azo dye.
